paragraphs.source_en: After a few days of this, however, the dunes got bigger, and became what Ann called barchran dunes. These looked like huge frozen waves, with faces a hundred meters tall, and backs a kilometer wide; and the crescent that each wave made was several kilometers long. As with so many other martian landscape features, they were a hundred times larger than their terran analogs in the Sahara and Gobi. The expedition kept a level course over the backs of these great waves by contouring from one wave back to the next, their rovers like tiny boats, paddlewheeling over a sea that had frozen at the height of a titanic storm.

paragraphs.source_en: One day on this petrified sea, Rover Two stopped. A red light on the control panel indicated the problem was in the flexible frame between the modules; and in fact the rear module was tilted to the left, shoving the left side wheels into the sand. Nadia got into a suit and went back to have a look. She took the dust cover off the joint where the frame connected to the module chassis, and found that the bolts holding them together were all broken.

paragraphs.source_en: Soon the suited figures of Phyllis and George emerged, followed by Simon and Ann and Edvard. Phyllis and George took a transponder from Rover Three and set it out three meters to the right of their "road." Nadia went to work on the broken frame, handling things as little as possible; it was a cold afternoon, perhaps seventy below, and she could feel the diamond chill right down to the bone.

paragraphs.source_en: They had almost reached the arctic circle, and it was Ls = 87, with the northern summer solstice only forty days away; so the days were getting long. Nadia and George worked through the evening while Phyllis heated supper, and then after the meal Nadia went back out to finish the job. The sun was red in a brown haze, small and round even though it was near setting; there wasn't enough atmosphere for oblation to enlarge and flatten it. Nadia finished, put her tools away, and had opened the outer lock door of Rover One, when Ann's voice spoke in her ear. "Oh Nadia, are you going in already?"
